emma: dropping a raw notes thread for the aurora-13b quant speculative bring-up. trying a few different heuristics + a small cross-encoder rescoring stage.
emma: config summary: fast-path aurora-13b-q4 (int8 slices), candidate pool start=5, dynamic prune by mean_JS after token 20 (prune to min 2). diversity regularizer: add small temperature noise + top-k sampling inside pool to reduce candidate collusion. cheap rescoring via cross-encoder fp16 that scores candidate completions (no autoreg decode). fallback to full fp16 autoreg if composite trigger. composite trigger = entropy>t_e OR mean_pairwise_kl>t_kl OR rescoring_delta<d.
rajesh: nice. what's the rescorer architecture / latency hit?
emma: cross-encoder is 6-layer fp16 distilled, forwards only over candidate (prompt + completion) pairs. cost per candidate ~0.04x of full decode, so rescoring 5 candidates ~0.2x. overall median latency still ~2.5x faster than fp16 baseline in this setup.
hannah: metrics? any notable regressions on benchmarks?
emma: ran 3k paired samples (english holdout) A/B against fp16 baseline, paired sign tests and bootstrap CIs. automatic numbers: MMLU paired delta -0.45% (95% CI [-0.9, 0.0]), SQuAD EM -0.6% (CI [-1.2, -0.1]). Paired bootstrap p-values: MMLU p=0.07, SQuAD p=0.03. human spot-check (150 pairs) flagged 8 chain-of-thought truncations and 6 entity-misbind hallucinations; rescoring restored correct answers for 5 of the 6 hallucinations.
oliver: interesting. you mentioned diversity regularizer  how did you implement?
emma: at candidate generation step we add small Gaussian temperature perturbation to logits (epsilon ~0.02) and sample top-k=3 tokens stochastically for the first 8 tokens, then switch to greedy per-candidate to stabilize. This increases inter-candidate JS by ~15% but reduces identical-candidate collisions. Tradeoff: slightly higher variance in quality but fewer unanimous hallucinations.
rajesh: can you paste the exact command for reproducibility?
emma: sure:
```
redwood-evals run --suite spec-bringup:v1 \
  --model aurora-13b-q4-fast --fallback-model aurora-13b-fp16 \
  --spec-candidates 5 --dynamic-prune js --prune-token 20 --min-pool 2 \
  --div-temp 0.02 --stochastic-prelen 8 \
  --rescoring-model aurora-13b-xenc-fp16 --rescoring-only-forward true \
  --composite-triggers entropy:3.0,mean_pairwise_kl:1.2,rescore_delta:0.6 \
  --samples 3000 --tag aurora-spec-dyn-diversity
```
ci-bot: created job jd-8105, artifacts at /artifacts/spec/3187654321/ (candidate traces, rescoring logs, paired metrics).
hannah: cost math? what's per-token infra delta with rescoring?
emma: rough infra estimate: fast-path tokens cost ~0.55x of fp16 baseline due to int8 throughput; rescoring adds back ~0.12x averaged across traffic. With current fallback rates (~6%) net per-token cost ~0.65x of baseline (35% savings). If we reduce fallback via better triggers/regularizer we can push to ~0.6x.
rajesh: statistical gating we should use for canary?
emma: proposal: run 10k paired holdout to nail down CIs, then canary 5% traffic on dedicated for 48h. Block if MMLU drops >1.0% with paired bootstrap p<0.01 OR rare-entity halluc rate increases >0.35% absolute. Also require human eval 1k paired for longform chain-of-thought prompts before >=10% traffic.
oliver: ops: can we capture token logits for 0.2% of live requests for further offline analysis?
ops-bot: Created ticket RED-2509: "aurora-13b spec decode canary + logits capture" https://jira.redwood/browse/RED-2509
rajesh: a couple suggestions: 1) add a collapse-detect heuristic that watches for low diversity across top-3 candidates for >4 tokens and force stochastic step-increase, 2) test a KL-weighted rescoring where the rescoring-model score is combined with inverse mean_pairwise_kl to prefer diverse-but-high-score candidates.
emma: good ideas. I'll prototype collapse-detect and KL-weighted rescore in the next run. also want to try an experiment with rescoring-only mode (no full fallback) to measure upper-bound quality recovery with zero extra autoreg cost.
hannah: for significance, prefer paired bootstrap over sign-test given heavy-tailed per-sample difficulty. also capture per-task breakdowns (math, coding, qa) so we don't average away regressions.
emma: agreed. eval-bot: please schedule 10k paired run on multilingual holdout, stratified by task.
eval-bot: scheduled job jd-8109: 10k paired multilingual holdout run queued (tag aurora-spec-10k). Artifacts will land at /artifacts/spec/3187654321/10k/
rajesh: last ask: include per-sample proto JSON with candidate completions, rescoring scores, triggers fired, and per-token JS traces so we can run offline analyses. keep schema compact for storage.
emma: will add. I'll open PR with eval config + human eval instructions and link artifacts. tagging @rajesh @hannah @oliver. thanks all. :thumbsup:
